newsitem.title: KENYA: Stocks recover in active trading at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Stocks recover in active trading at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index recovered on Friday boosted by heavy trading of shares on the three-days special board, brokers said.
The index rose 8.47 points to stand at 3073.88 while turnover jumped to 31.257 million shillings on 1,140,800 shares compared to 6.295 million shillings on 238,733 shares on Thursday.
The market's turnover was driven high by heaving trading in shares on the three-days special board for Housing Finance Company and National Bank of Kenya.
Housing Finance Company traded a total of 502,183 shares at 30 shillings from a previous 25 while National Bank of Kenya dealt 456,170 shares at 18.50 from 17.30.
Kenya Commercial Bank rose to 56 from 55.50 while Standard Chartered Bank gained to 47 from 46.50.
A senior broker said strong on Friday activity resulted from the high volumes traded on the special board. He added that such volumes on average lifted a market that had begun the week low.
Brokers said Kenya Airways was on it's way up, after advancing marginally on improved demand. The airline was helped by news that supply was too thin.
"This is because most people are still holding back their share. Most of the speculators have already sold out there shares as they wanted to get out of the stock," he said.
Kenya Airways traded a total of 33,477 shares at 10.65, 10.10 and 10.60 from 10.50, CMC Holding rose a shilling to 61 while Uchumi Supermarket was unchanged at 39.
Most plantations held steady: Brooke Bond at 176, Rea Vipingo at 11.20 and Sasini Tea & Coffee rose to 51 from 50.
Crown Berger continued to react negatively to a company report that it made a 15.4 million shilling loss in the first six months to 30 June 1996. Crown Berger dropped 4.0 shillings to 10.
Brokers said most people were becoming very wary of companies that posted losses and Crown Berger had just done that.
